questions.question: Two reviewers independently found that note 7 ("shared decisions most often retrofitted") and Q4's Retries row went to OP-01 only. But shared.md gives missing-key delete to OP-10's flow, a streamed-write exception to OP-03's flow, and retry to each entry's AX-13. Retries also names "GCS retries deletes by default". The agreed scope sent Q4's shared rows and note 7 to OP-01 only. How should those passages be routed?

options.label: Route by shared.md (Recommended)
options.description: Note 7 is also copied into OP-03 and OP-10, and the Retries row into OP-10. The rule becomes: a passage goes to every entry whose operation it names, or that shared.md makes its home. That rule is stated in BACKLOG-DONE. Error taxonomy, Timeouts and Consistency stay OP-01-only (shared.md homes them in OP-01's flow and RFC-0027 P3). Retries for every other entry's AX-13 is not copied 24 times.

options.label: Keep OP-01 only, state why
options.description: No files change. BACKLOG-DONE and the trace state that note 7 and Q4's cross-cutting rows go to OP-01, the first session, and that later sessions read shared.md for their home. That narrows the "each input file with a § 2 finding" claim. OP-10 and OP-03 sessions then never see the evidence.

options.label: Copy all Q4 rows by name
options.description: Apply 'names the operation' to every Q4 row as well. Consistency's "atomic put" goes to OP-03 and OP-04, and "list may miss recent writes" to OP-06 and OP-07, on top of the recommended routing. This widens the PR, and judging which row names which operation invites further rounds.
